summary: C2 is implemented: the lexer marks each word as expanded or literal, the judge refuses expanded words wherever it reads structure, xargs gets the appended or replace-string word, and match tries expanded words as any text after the as-written pass. Gate T2 passes 108 of 109 cases. The one miss is a gate case that contradicts acceptance 3.

notes: Per-byte quote state (stUnquoted, stDouble, stLiteral) in the lexer feeds expands(); command.exp runs parallel to words and plain. internal/fence/expand.go holds match (as written, then any-text), skipXargs, shellString, xargsCommand and the NFA intersection used to decide whether a rule and a command with wildcard words share a string. gate_dispute.reason: The gate case `review git remote $X` expects the fence rule `Bash(git remote add:*)` with the any-text suffix. The command as written already matches the Copilot stem `git remote:*`, so acceptance 3 (as-written match first, with today's rules and messages) gives the stem message.
gate_dispute.evidence: cases.tsv row `review\tgit remote $X` wants `git remote $X is denied by the review fence (Bash(git remote add:*)): a word the shell expands may be any text`. internal/driver/agent_copilot.go:24 lists `git remote:*` among the stems, and `git remote $X` has the prefix `git remote `, so the first pass matches it. Today's output is `git remote $X is denied by the Copilot deny list (git remote:*)`. Producing the fence message would mean skipping the as-written pass for the stems.
